title: Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management: SMAPE accuracy and AI explanations for Demand planning forecasts
summary: Hold: the briefing understates documented row-level security and omits the manager and administrator exceptions to Contributor restrictions. Its claim that Microsoft does not explain how to update an existing installation is also too broad; the platform documents app updates, although a version-specific rollout schedule remains unconfirmed.

claims.where: controls[1].ui; Governance controls table
claims.claim: Security roles are managed in Power Platform admin center through Manage > Environments > environment > Settings > Users + permissions > Users > user > Manage security roles.
claims.quote: Select Settings. ... Select Users + permissions, and then select Users. ... On the Users page select a user, and then select Manage security roles.

claims.where: controls[1].api; Governance controls table
claims.claim: The printed POST to the v9.0 systemuserroles_association/$ref endpoint assigns a security role to the identified user.
claims.quote: POST [Organization URI]/api/data/v9.0/systemusers(azureactivedirectoryobjectid=<user object ID>)/systemuserroles_association/$ref

claims.where: controls[1].note; Governance controls table
claims.claim: The security-role association request identifies the role through @odata.id.
claims.quote: "@odata.id":"[Organization URI]/api/data/v9.0/roles(<role ID>)"

claims.where: Scope: Roles that manage access
claims.claim: System Administrator has the required security-role assignment privileges by default.
claims.quote: By default, the System Administrator security role has all the required privileges to assign security roles to any user, including assigning the System Administrator security role.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Scope; Governance controls
claims.claim: Power Platform accounts with Demand Planning Contributor, Demand Planning Manager or System Administrator roles can access Demand planning.
claims.quote: To be able to access Demand planning, users must sign in a Power Platform user account that has the security roles for the features they need.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance controls
claims.claim: Demand Planning Contributors see only data granted by row-level rules and no data by default, without qualification for other assigned roles.
claims.quote: Users who have the Demand Planning Contributor role (but not Demand Planning Manager or System Administrator) can access Demand planning, but they can only view and edit data that they're granted access to.
claims.fix: Qualify both statements: 'Users with Demand Planning Contributor, but not Demand Planning Manager or System Administrator, can view and edit only data granted by row-level access rules and see no data by default.' Retain the existing users-access citation.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Open questions: row-level access
claims.claim: Microsoft has not said whether row-level access rules apply to the calculation accuracy page.
claims.quote: Users who have the Demand Planning Contributor role (but not Demand Planning Manager or System Administrator) can access Demand planning, but they can only view and edit data that they're granted access to.
claims.fix: Remove the sentence saying Microsoft has not confirmed row-level access for this page and remove that Open questions bullet. The documented app-wide rule already covers Contributors without the Manager or System Administrator roles; retain the practical test-account recommendation as validation advice.
